source.publication: 2025 DR 0104 Booklet (Colorado Individual Income Tax), DR 0104 and DR 0104AD
source.section: DR 0104AD line 3 / line 5 Social Security Benefits (PDF p.18 Line 3; p.19 Line 5; DR 0104AD p.1 lines 3 and 5), joint federal AGI 'did not exceed $95,000' (exactly 95,000 qualifies); DR 0104 lines 1, 10-13 (PDF p.8, p.10); tax table PDF p.34-35

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (spouse) 69,500.00 + taxable Social Security 25,500.00 = 95,000.00. Taxable Social Security on gross benefits 30,000.00 (you): federal SS worksheet (given): half of benefits 15,000.00 + other income 69,500.00 = 84,500.00; less 32,000.00 = 52,500.00; line 11 = 40,500.00; line 13 = half of smaller of 52,500.00 and 12,000.00 = 6,000.00; line 14 = 6,000.00; line 15 = 85% x 40,500.00 = 34,425.00; line 16 = 40,425.00; 85% of benefits = 25,500.00; taxable Social Security = 25,500.00. Federal taxable income = 95,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 63,500.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). DR 0104 line 1 federal taxable income (Form 1040 line 15) 63,500.00; lines 2-9 additions 0.00 (no state income tax addback, no other-state bond interest; federal AGI 95,000.00 is not over 300,000, so no line 4 deduction addback); line 10 subtotal 63,500.00. DR 0104AD: Line 3 (primary taxpayer, age 64, 55-64): federal AGI (DR 0104 line 34) 95,000.00 does not exceed 95,000.00 (married filing jointly), so the entire taxable Social Security 25,500.00 (better than the 20,000-limited subtraction, smaller of 25,500.00 and 20,000.00 = 20,000.00). Line 22 subtotal = 25,500.00; DR 0104 line 11 = 25,500.00. Line 12 Colorado taxable income = 63,500.00 - 25,500.00 = 38,000.00. Line 13 tax = 4.4% x 38,000.00 = 1,672.00 (the tax table row over 37,900.00 but not over 38,000.00, PDF p.35, gives 1,670.00; expected keeps the formula figure). No credits claimed: 0.00. Colorado income tax 1,672.00. Edge: federal AGI is exactly 95,000.00; the booklet's test is 'did not exceed $95,000', so the full subtraction still applies at the threshold. Joint return with one Social Security recipient: the whole Form 1040 line 6b amount is the primary taxpayer's, so no split between spouses is needed; the spouse (58, wages only) has no subtraction.
accepted_approximations: Tax is figured on the exact income at 4.4%; below 50,000 the booklet uses the tax table, which taxes each 100-dollar row at its midpoint and rounds to the dollar.
